correctness.rationale: For each prime \(\ell\), equality of outputs is equality of the vectors \((\max(v_\ell(e_i),v_\ell(\alpha)))_i\). With \(m=\min_i v_\ell(e_i)=v_\ell(h)\), this vector records exactly \(\max(v_\ell(\alpha)-m,0)\), which is the \(\ell\)-adic valuation of \(\alpha/\gcd(\alpha,h)\). The converse is identical prime by prime. The fiber formula follows by solving these valuation constraints, and the injectivity statement follows from the \(s=1\) fiber. The embedded verifier independently checks 2,714,400 parameter instances and 7,900 closed-fiber instances without finding a violation. Risk: the finite replay is not an infinite proof; correctness rests on the prime-adic argument given in RESULT.md.

originality.rationale: The 2023 focal paper proves only the special output fiber \(g_\alpha(n)=n\), equivalent to \(\alpha\mid h\), plus composition and other properties. The inspected 2025 follow-up studies compositions, inequalities, and an equivalence relation that varies the base integer; it does not classify collisions between two parameters for one fixed base integer. Targeted public literature searches found no statement implying the normalized-parameter criterion or its fiber cardinalities. A previously checked result classifies the gcd-exponent companion \(f_\alpha\), whose invariant is \(\gcd(\alpha,L)\) with \(L=\operatorname{lcm}(e_i)\); that result does not imply the present lcm-exponent theorem, whose invariant instead uses the gcd of the exponents and whose image is infinite.

value.rationale: The focal source singles out the finiteness of the special equation \(g_\alpha(n)=n\). The new theorem naturally completes that question from one output fiber to every output collision, gives exact fiber sizes, an injectivity criterion, and shows that the lcm-exponent family has an infinite parameter image despite finite fibers. This is a structural classification of the parameterization, not a chosen numerical slice. It also reveals a qualitative contrast with the gcd-exponent companion: finite periodic orbit versus infinite image with explicitly controlled collisions. Risk: the proof is elementary and the theorem is narrow to this arithmetic-function family; its value is completeness and structure rather than a downstream application.
